Ectodermal dysplasia with osteosclerosis and Crouzon-related skeletal abnormalities; no supplied evidence establishes other common organ damage.
Inherited fatty-acid oxidation and ketogenesis disorders; hepatic, cardiac and muscle injury vary substantially across subtypes.
Spinal neural-tube and vertebral closure defects; neurogenic bladder affects most clinically significant cases (~70–90% of open forms), though closed forms vary.
Congenital structural foot deformity; CNS and palate findings from small syndromic families do not characterize most clubfoot patients.
Sinoatrial node dysfunction causes bradycardia and tachyarrhythmia; syncope and dizziness do not establish neurologic damage.

Congenital skeletal myopathy; common ventilatory failure reflects respiratory muscle weakness. Eye abnormalities are nonspecific; pneumonia is a separate complication.

Nasal skeletal hypoplasia and epiphyseal stippling define embryopathy; intellectual disability occurs in 30–79%. Cardiac and ocular malformations occur in 5–29%.
Cutaneous necrobiotic histiocytic lesions; periorbital skin disease alone is not ocular damage. Destructive ocular involvement is not reliably ≥30%; gammopathy is separate.

Cardiac dysrhythmia abruptly reduces cardiac output; transient syncope or convulsive movements do not establish neurologic damage.
